{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-tn","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"f01a56adcfa68434eaf928503d366e3bc678a9488f9e4b594d262f98254bfa36","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-tn-class-d:lineage:14","source_registry_sha256":"8b0b6a068a0aa720d419171b5007a2610ed6c5012eeff522b57713cf9226eb71","source_liveness_sha256":"d27b9a94f03ec29d960b8eea38966606a7d3fdb703ad30b19ecd93f9bc70d0c7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"The examinations: vision, knowledge and road tests","heading":"C — The examinations: which tests apply, vision screening, the knowledge test format and rules, retake waits, road test appointments, vehicle equipment, scoring and immediate failure","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — The examinations: which tests apply, vision screening, the knowledge test format and rules, retake waits, road test appointments, vehicle equipment, scoring and immediate failure
Knowledge domain: what the Tennessee driver license examination consists of and how it is run — which tests each applicant type takes, the vision standard, the knowledge test format, languages and conduct rules, waiting periods after a failure, road test appointments, the equipment a test vehicle must have, how road test errors are scored and what causes immediate failure.

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
The Tennessee driver license examination has three parts: a vision screening, a knowledge test and a road test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Every Driver Service Center gives license tests except the express service centers, and knowledge tests are handled first-come, first-served. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Road tests take long enough to administer that they are given only by appointment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
Road tests are not given in extreme weather such as heavy rain or snow, dense fog, hail, high winds or icy roads, and in the winter months they are not given after dark. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
No test may be repeated on the same day it was taken. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
Each time you take and fail a PD, D or H test you pay the $2 application fee again. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
An original Class D or Class H applicant takes the knowledge test, the road skills test and the vision screening, while a Class PD applicant takes only the vision screening and knowledge test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
A new resident with a current, valid out-of-state license takes only the vision screening, but one whose license is expired, or who comes from another country or never held a license, takes all three tests. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A01
The vision screening requires at least 20/40 vision in each eye alone and in both eyes together, with or without glasses or contact lenses. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A01
An applicant who cannot pass the vision screening must have an eye specialist of their choice complete an eye statement for the Department to evaluate. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A01
The knowledge test is multiple choice, built from Sections B and C of the manual, and is expected to split roughly 25% each among traffic signs and signals, safe driving principles, rules of the road, and drugs and alcohol. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A01
Knowledge tests run on computerized testing machines, with written versions only in very limited cases, and computerized centers also offer Spanish, Korean and Japanese versions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A01
An applicant whose first language is not English may use a translation dictionary free of notes or handwriting, but phones, PDAs and electronic dictionaries are banned and interpreters may not help with any test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A01
Oral knowledge tests are offered by appointment at selected centers for applicants who cannot read or have a learning disability, and an applicant under 18 must first supply a physician's or educational specialist's written statement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A01
Any cheating on a required examination means automatic failure and a 30-day wait before the test may be attempted again. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A02
After failing any knowledge test you must wait at least one day before trying again, and the same wait applies after every later failure. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A02
Road test applicants must speak and understand enough English to communicate with the examiner during the drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A02
You must supply your own road test vehicle, with all its operating equipment and safety features in working order. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A02
Arriving more than 5 minutes late for a road test appointment cancels the test, and you must reschedule for a later date. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A02
Road tests go ahead in light to moderate rain, fog or snow but not in heavy rain, thunderstorms, thick fog, flooded or snow- and ice-packed roads, or during severe weather warnings. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A02
Any passenger vehicle built in 1969 or later must have safety belts in good working condition for both the applicant and the examiner. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A02
By law every car needs two separate ways to apply the brakes: a regular foot brake and a parking brake. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A02
A motor vehicle must carry at least two and no more than four white headlights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A02
A passenger vehicle needs a rear license plate light, two red tail lights and two red brake lights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A02
A vehicle with a windshield should have 2 wipers, unless a single wiper clears to within 1 inch of the inside of the windshield. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A02
The test vehicle needs at least one rearview mirror that does not block the driver's rear view, and two outside mirrors are also required for applicants with certain vision or hearing impairments. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A02
Road test appointments can be booked online or by toll-free phone up to 45 days ahead of the desired test date. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A02
You must already have passed the knowledge test before your road test appointment, or the appointment is canceled. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A02
Plan to arrive at least 15 minutes before the road test appointment so paperwork and documents can be processed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A03
No tint may be applied to the windshield, and on a passenger car no window material may let through less than 35% of visible light. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A03
Passenger car bumpers must sit 14 to 22 inches above the ground, and 4x4 recreational vehicle bumpers 14 to 31 inches. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A03
Only the applicant and the examiner, or other authorized personnel, may ride in the road test vehicle, no animal is allowed, and you will never be asked to do anything illegal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A03
A road test ends in immediate failure for any traffic law violation, refusing to cooperate or follow directions, any dangerous action, or contributing to an accident. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A03
On the road test, 1 to 6 errors is a pass, 7 to 9 errors means a retest the next day, 10 to 12 errors means seven days, and 13 to 15 errors means fourteen days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A03
Sixteen or more road test errors, or an automatic failure, means a 30-day practice period before a retest. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A04
Road tests average 20 to 25 minutes, and arriving five or more minutes late means the appointment must be rescheduled. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F37 | anchor: A04
Teens aged 15 to 17 who must take the written test may take it online, supervised by a parent or legal guardian acting as proctor through the Tennessee Proctor Identification (PID) App. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

Misconceptions: an interpreter may not help with any license test even though a translation dictionary is allowed; failing a knowledge test means at least a one-day wait, not a same-day retry; the road test can be failed before driving if the vehicle lacks required equipment; a road test can end at once for a single traffic law violation.
Mnemonics: twenty-forty in each eye and both together; same day never, next day at the earliest; pass with six errors or fewer.
Glossary: vision screening means the eyesight check required before any license or permit; road skills test means the driving test given with an examiner; express service center means a center that does not give license tests; PID App means the Tennessee Proctor Identification app used for online knowledge tests.
Dynamic facts: appointment systems, phone numbers, the online proctored test program, the language list and the application fee can change; confirm them on the Department of Safety and Homeland Security website before showing them to learners.
